description: Functional and non-functional requirements take separate ID sequences. The email deadline is a threshold on a behaviour, so it is split into an FR and an NFR; the WCAG level is an NFR. Each sequence starts at 001.

must_match.pattern: ^FR-001: When a guest submits the booking form, the booking service shall send a confirmation email
must_match.why: the behaviour is functional and the FR sequence starts at 001
the NFR sequence starts at 001, not after the last FR

must_match.pattern: ^NFR-\d+: [^\n]*the booking service shall send a confirmation email[^\n]*within 2 minutes of the submission
must_match.why: the deadline is a non-functional requirement with its starting point

must_match.pattern: ^NFR-\d+: The booking web app shall (comply with|conform to|meet) WCAG 2\.2 level AA\.

must_not_match.why: the deadline is a threshold on the response: an NFR, not part of the FR
each sequence counts its own requirements: two of each

manual: The NFR for the email deadline names the event its 2 minutes start from.
FR lines come before NFR lines, and questions come last.
